label: Sample Exam Set B
source: ISTQB CTFL v4.0 Sample Exam B, Questions v1.7 / Answers v1.7 (istqb.org)

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of why testing is necessary?
o: Dynamic testing increases quality by causing test objects to fail in ways that could never be achieved by the users
Static testing is used by developers to identify failures in their code earlier than can be achieved through dynamic testing
Static analysis provides evidence to customers that the elements of the system that provide no outputs are fit for release
Reviews increase the quality of requirements specifications and lead to fewer changes being needed in derived work products
questions.e: Reviews are static testing that starts at the very beginning of the SDLC and removes defects in requirements before design and code depend on them. Static testing finds defects, not failures, and static analysis results are for developers rather than customers.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about quality assurance (QA) and/or quality control (QC) is correct?
o: QA is performed as part of testing
Testing is performed as part of QC
Testing is another term for QC
Testing is performed as part of QA
questions.e: QA takes a preventive approach and concentrates on process improvement, while testing is a form of quality control that detects and helps correct defects. QC also uses non-testing techniques such as model checking, proofs and simulation.

questions.q: One of the 'principles of testing' states that exhaustive testing is impossible. Which of the following is an example of addressing this principle in practice?
o: Creating test cases that cover every possible specified output
Documenting all possible test input variations and prioritizing these based on importance
Starting testing as early as possible with reviews and other static testing approaches
Using equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis to generate test cases
questions.e: Techniques such as equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis derive a finite, systematic subset of the practically infinite set of possible tests. Documenting all variations is impractical and early static testing addresses a different principle.

questions.q: Which test activity involves working with test data requirements, test conditions, test environment requirements and test cases?
questions.e: Test design turns test conditions into test cases and other testware such as test data requirements and test environment requirements. Execution runs procedures, analysis defines test conditions, and implementation builds procedures, schedules and environments.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to impact how testing is performed for a given test object?
o: The average level of experience of the organization's marketing team
The knowledge of users that a new system is being developed for them
The number of years' experience of the members of the test team
The end user's organizational structure for a commercial music streaming application
questions.e: The experience of the test team decides the capabilities, tools and techniques they can apply, which directly shapes how testing is performed. The other factors are largely unrelated to the test approach.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is a CORRECT example of the value of traceability?
o: Traceability between the mitigated risks and test cases that passed provides a means of determining the level of residual risk
Traceability between user requirements and test results provides a means of measuring project progress against business goals
Traceability between testers and test cases that failed provides a means of determining the skill level of the testers
Traceability between the identified risks and written test conditions provides a means of determining which risks are worth testing
questions.e: Linking requirements to test results shows which requirements have been tested, which measures progress against business goals. Residual risk needs traceability from all risks, tester metrics are counter-productive, and deciding which risks are worth testing is risk management.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be an example of a tester using a generic skill when testing?
o: The tester's deep knowledge of a variety of computer games meant that they got on well with one of the developers who was also into gaming
The tester was a former pilot and was better able to understand the acceptance criteria for the helicopter control system
The tester previously worked as a programmer and used their skills in this area to better communicate with the business analysts
The tester was very careful not to make mistakes when they methodically generated test cases prior to starting their exploratory testing session
questions.e: Domain knowledge that helps a tester understand and communicate with end users and business representatives is a generic tester skill, as with the former pilot on a helicopter control system. In exploratory testing the test cases are created during the session, not scripted beforehand.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole-team approach?
o: It allows team members to take on any role at any time
It only needs a single team to support the complete development project
It embeds business representatives alongside developers in the same team
It generates a team synergy that benefits the entire project
questions.e: Using each member's skills effectively creates synergy, better collaboration and better communication. Team members only take roles they are competent in, and the approach says nothing about how many teams a project needs.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the chosen software development lifecycle is CORRECT?
o: If agile software development is used, automation of system tests replaces the need for regression testing
If a sequential development model is used, then the dynamic testing is typically restricted to later in the lifecycle
If an iterative development model is used, then component testing is typically performed manually by developers
If an incremental development model is used, then static testing is done in early increments and dynamic testing in later increments
questions.e: In a sequential model no executable code exists early, so dynamic testing happens later while static testing and test preparation happen early. Agile still needs regression testing, iterative models favour automated component tests, and increments need both static and dynamic testing.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
o: Testers should review work products as part of the next development phase
Testers should review work products as soon as drafts are available
Testers should review work products before test analysis and test design begin
Testers should review work products immediately after they are published
questions.e: Shift-left means reviewing work products as soon as drafts exist, so defects are removed before later work depends on them, rather than waiting for the next phase or for publication.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?
questions.e: Test-Driven Development is the well-known test-first approach where tests are written before the code. Feature-Driven Development is an agile methodology, and the other two names are not test-first approaches.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about DevOps is CORRECT?
o: To speed up releases, continuous integration is used to encourage developers to submit code quickly without the need to complete component testing
To be able to update and release systems on a more frequent basis, many automated regression tests are required to reduce the risk of regression
To treat both developers and operations equally, the testers will allocate more effort to release testing by operations using a shift-right approach
To create increased synergy between testers, developers and operations, the testing must become fully automated with no manual testing
questions.e: Frequent delivery in DevOps needs extensive automated regression testing to keep regression risk low. Component tests must pass before code is admitted to the build, testers do not shift effort to operations, and manual testing remains valuable.

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be performed as part of system testing?
o: Security testing of a credit management system by an independent test team
Testing the interface of a currency exchange system with an external banking system
Beta testing of a remote learning system by courseware developers
Testing interactions between the user interface and database of a human resources system
questions.e: System testing examines the behaviour and non-functional characteristics of the complete system, often by an independent team, so security testing of the whole credit management system fits. External interfaces are system integration testing, beta testing is acceptance testing, and UI-database interaction is component integration testing.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
o: Regression tests increase in number as the project progresses, whereas the number of confirmation tests decreases as the project progresses
Regression tests are created and run when the test object is fixed, whereas confirmation tests are run whenever the test object is enhanced
Regression testing is concerned with checking that the operational environment remains unchanged, whereas confirmation testing is concerned with testing changes to the test object
Regression testing is concerned with adverse effects in unchanged code, whereas confirmation testing is concerned with testing changed code
questions.e: Regression testing checks that changes have not harmed unchanged software, while confirmation testing verifies that a specific defect has been fixed, which means testing changed code. Both kinds of test normally grow as the project progresses.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a defect that can be found by static testing but NOT by dynamic testing?
o: Lack of usability provided through the user interface
Code with no path that reaches it
Poor response times for most of the expected users
Required features that are not implemented in the code
questions.e: A code review can reveal unreachable code, while dynamic tests only exercise reachable code. Usability, response times and missing features can all be exposed by running the software.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback?
o: Managers are aware of which developers are less productive
It allows project managers to prioritize their stakeholder interactions
It facilitates early communication of potential quality issues
End users better understand why the delivery of the work product is delayed
questions.e: Feedback from stakeholders early and often communicates potential quality issues sooner, also preventing requirement misunderstandings and costly rework.

questions.q:
Match the review task descriptions (1-4) with the review activities (A-D):
1. The quality characteristics to be evaluated and the exit criteria are selected
2. Everyone has access to the work product
3. Anomalies are identified in the work product
4. Anomalies are discussed
A. Individual review
B. Review initiation
C. Planning
D. Communication and analysis
questions.e: Planning selects scope, quality characteristics and exit criteria (1C), review initiation ensures access to the work product and clarifies roles (2B), individual review identifies and logs anomalies (3A), and communication and analysis discusses and decides on them (4D).

questions.q:
Match the review roles (1-4) with their responsibilities (A-D):
1. Scribe
2. Review leader
3. Facilitator
4. Manager
A. Ensures the effective running of review meetings and the setting up of a safe review environment
B. Records review information, such as decisions and new anomalies found during the review meeting
C. Decides what is to be reviewed and provides resources, such as staff and time for the review
D. Takes overall responsibility for the review such as organizing when and where the review will take place
questions.e: The scribe records decisions and anomalies (1B), the review leader takes overall responsibility and organizes the review (2D), the facilitator or moderator keeps meetings effective and safe (3A), and the manager decides what is reviewed and provides resources (4C).

questions.q: Which of the following statements BEST describes the difference between decision table testing and branch testing?
o: In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from the decision statements in the code. In branch testing, the test cases are derived from knowledge of the control flow of the test object.

In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from the specification that describes the business logic. In branch testing the test cases are based on anticipation of potential defects in the source code.

In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from knowledge of the control flow of the test object. In branch testing, test cases are derived from the specification that describes the business logic.
In decision table testing, the test cases are independent of how the software is implemented. In branch testing, test cases can be created only after the design or implementation of the code.
questions.e: Decision table testing is black-box, so its test cases come from the specified business logic and do not depend on the implementation; branch testing is white-box, so its test cases need the design or code to exist. Anticipation of defects is error guessing.

questions.q:
Customers of the TestWash car wash chain have cards with a record of the number of washes bought so far, starting at 0. After entering the car wash, the system increases the number by one and this value is the number of the current wash. For every tenth wash the system gives a 10% discount, and for every twentieth wash a further 40% discount (a 50% discount in total).
Which set of input data (the numbers of the current wash) achieves the highest equivalence partition coverage?
questions.e: The valid partitions are no discount, 10% discount (multiples of 10) and 50% discount (multiples of 20). Option a covers all three: 19 (no discount), 20 (50%) and 30 (10%). The other options leave at least one partition uncovered.

questions.q: A form verifies the length of a password: the length is correct between 6 and 12 characters inclusive, otherwise it is incorrect, and the form starts empty (password length = 0). Your test set achieves 100% 2-value boundary value coverage. Because of the high risk, the team decided to add test cases for 100% 3-value boundary value coverage. Which additional password lengths should be tested?
questions.e: The partitions are {0..5}, {6..12} and {13, 14, ...}. Full 3-value BVA needs 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 14; 2-value BVA already covered 0, 5, 6, 12 and 13, so the missing lengths are 1, 4, 7, 11 and 14.

questions.q:
A decision table determines atherosclerosis risk. Rule 1: cholesterol <= 124, blood pressure <= 140, risk very low. Rule 2: cholesterol <= 124, blood pressure > 140, risk low. Rule 3: cholesterol 125-200, blood pressure <= 140, risk medium. Rule 4: cholesterol 125-200, blood pressure > 140, risk high. Rule 5: cholesterol >= 201, risk very high.
Test cases: TC1 cholesterol 125, pressure 141; TC2 cholesterol 200, pressure 201; TC3 cholesterol 124, pressure 201; TC4 cholesterol 109, pressure 200; TC5 cholesterol 201, pressure 140.
What is the decision table coverage achieved by these test cases?
questions.e: TC1 and TC2 both cover Rule 4, TC3 and TC4 both cover Rule 2, and TC5 covers Rule 5, so three of the five rules are covered: 3/5 = 60%.

questions.q: A storage system can store up to three elements and is modeled by a state transition diagram, where N is the number of currently stored elements. Which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, achieves the highest level of valid transitions coverage?
o: Add, Add, Add, Add, Remove, Remove
questions.e: Option c exercises Add while not full, Add that reaches FULL, Remove from FULL, Remove while not full, and an invalid-free path through five transitions, so it covers all five valid transitions. Option b is infeasible because no Add transition leaves FULL, and options a and d cover only four of the five.

questions.q: You run two test cases, T1 and T2, on the same code. Test T1 achieved 40% statement coverage and test T2 achieved 65% statement coverage. Which of the following sentences must be necessarily true?
o: The test suite composed of tests T1 and T2 achieves 105% statement coverage
There exists at least one statement that must have been executed by both T1 and T2
At least 5% of the statements in the code that was tested are non-executable
The test suite composed of tests T1 and T2 achieves full branch coverage
questions.e: Coverage can never exceed 100%, so 40% + 65% cannot be disjoint: at least 5% of statements were executed by both tests. Statement coverage says nothing about non-executable statements or about branch coverage.

questions.q: Let the branch coverage metric be defined as BCov = (X / Y) * 100%. What do X and Y represent in this formula?
o: X = number of decision outcomes exercised by the test cases, Y = total number of decision outcomes in the code
X = number of conditional branches exercised by the test cases, Y = total number of branches in the code
X = number of branches exercised by the test cases, Y = total number of branches in the code
X = number of conditional branches exercised by the test cases, Y = total number of decision outcomes in the code
questions.e: A branch is any transfer of control between two nodes in the control flow graph, conditional or unconditional, so branch coverage is the number of branches exercised divided by the total number of branches.

questions.q: Which TWO of the following statements provide the BEST rationale for using exploratory testing?
o: Testers have not been allocated enough time for test design and test execution
The existing test strategy requires that testers use formal, black-box test techniques
The specification is written in a formal language that can be processed by a tool
Testers are the members of an agile team and have good programming skills
Testers are experienced in the business domain and have good analytical skills
questions.e: Exploratory testing suits time pressure and few or inadequate specifications, and it works best with experienced testers who have domain knowledge, analytical skills, curiosity and creativity. It is not a formal black-box technique and programming skill is irrelevant to it.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST fits as an element of the checklist used in checklist-based testing?
o: The developer made an error when implementing the code
The program works correctly regarding functional and non-functional requirements
The error messages are written in language that the user can understand
questions.e: A checklist should hold concrete test conditions a human can verify, such as the readability of error messages. Errors are not test conditions, coverage targets are exit criteria, and the third item is a whole test objective.

questions.q: Consider this acceptance criterion for a user story written from the perspective of an online store owner: 'Given that the user is logged in and on the homepage, When the user clicks on the Add Item button, Then the Create Item form should appear, And the user should be able to input a name and price for the new item.' In what format is this acceptance criteria written?
questions.e: Given/When/Then describes a scenario to be verified, so the format is scenario-oriented. Rule-oriented formats use bullet lists or tabulated input-output mappings.

questions.q: Your team analyzes the user story: As a registered customer, I want to be able to view my previous orders on the company's website, so that I can keep track of my purchases. Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?
o: Input: the customer logs into their account and clicks the see order history button. Expected: the system shows a list of all the customer's previous orders, including date, order number and total cost
Input: the customer clicks on an order from the order list. Expected: the system displays the individual items purchased, with their prices and quantities
Input: the customer clicks Sort ascending on the order history screen. Expected: the system shows the order history sorted by order number in ascending order
Input: an unregistered customer registers as a new customer with a valid e-mail address that does not already exist. Expected: the system accepts the registration and creates the account
questions.e: The user story is about viewing previous orders, and the first three test cases all exercise order history. Registration is a different feature and is not covered by this story.

questions.q: Your team follows a DevOps delivery pipeline whose first three steps are: (1) code development, (2) submit code into a version control system and merge it into the test branch, (3) perform component testing for the submitted code. Which of the following is BEST suited to be the entry criterion for step (2)?
o: Static analysis returns no high severity warnings for the submitted code
System version control reports no conflicts when merging code into the test branch
Component tests are compiled and ready to be executed
questions.e: Static analysis with no high severity warnings must be true before code is submitted and merged. Merge conflicts can only be seen after step 2, compiled component tests belong to step 3, and coverage is an exit criterion.

questions.q: You estimate test effort using estimation based on ratios. Historical data (development effort / test effort): P1 800,000 / 40,000; P2 1,200,000 / 130,000; P3 600,000 / 70,000; P4 1,000,000 / 120,000. The estimated development effort for the new project is $800,000. What is your estimate of the test effort?
questions.e: Average development effort is $900,000 and average test effort is $90,000, a ratio of 1:10, so test effort is 10% of development effort: 10% of $800,000 = $80,000.

questions.q:
You are testing a web application to SEARCH products, VIEW product details, ADD products to a shopping cart and place an ORDER. Test cases and priorities (1 = highest priority): TC1 SEARCH product A (4), TC2 SEARCH product B (4), TC3 VIEW product A (3), TC4 VIEW product B (2), TC5 ADD product A (3), TC6 ADD product B (1), TC7 place an ORDER (5).
Logical dependencies: SEARCH must be tested before VIEW, VIEW before ADD, ADD before ORDER. Which test case should be executed as the fourth one?
questions.e: Product B has higher priority, so the order starts TC2, TC4, TC6. The flow for product A must then be completed before ORDER, so TC1 is executed fourth, followed by TC3, TC5 and finally TC7.

questions.q: According to the testing quadrants model, which of the following falls into quadrant Q1 (technology facing, support the team)?
questions.e: Q1 holds technology facing tests that guide development, such as component and component integration testing. Usability and user acceptance testing are business facing and critique the product (Q3), and functional testing is business facing and supports the team (Q2).

questions.q:
Match the risks (1-4) with the mitigation activities (A-D):
1. Ineffective loop implementation causes long system responses
2. Consumers change their preferences
3. Flooding of the server room
4. Patients above a certain age receive inaccurate reports
A. Risk acceptance
B. Testing for performance efficiency
C. Using boundary value analysis as the test technique
D. Risk transfer
questions.e: Slow responses are addressed by performance efficiency testing (1B), changing consumer preferences are outside the team's control so the risk is accepted (2A), flooding is transferred through insurance (3D), and the age boundary is tested with BVA (4C).

questions.q: Which of the following is a product quality metric?
questions.e: Mean time to failure measures a quality characteristic, maturity, so it is a product quality metric. The others are defect metrics or coverage metrics.

questions.q: You are in a test team located in North America developing a product for a client in Europe. The team is agile, follows DevOps and uses a CI/CD pipeline. Which of the following is the LEAST effective way to communicate test progress to the customer?
questions.e: Face-to-face communication is the least effective here because the client is in a different location and time zone. Dashboards, email and video conferencing all work across the distance.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes an example of how configuration management (CM) supports testing?
o: Having the version number of the environment, the CM tool can retrieve the version numbers of libraries, stubs and drivers used in that environment
Having a record of the values of the inputs, the CM tool can execute the test cases for these configurations and calculate the coverage
Having data about the date of purchase of a software license, the CM tool automatically generates information about the fact that the product license is coming to an end
Having the version number of the test case, the CM tool can automatically generate test data for this test case
questions.e: For a complex configuration item such as a test environment, CM records the items it consists of, their relationships and their versions, which is exactly what option a describes. CM tools do not execute tests, manage licences or generate test data.

questions.q: You test a sort function that returns a set of numbers sorted in ascending order. The log shows: TC1 input 3, output 3, passed; TC2 input 3 11 6 5, output 3 5 6 11, passed; TC3 input 8 7 3 7 1, output 1 3 7 8, failed; TC4 input -2 -2 -2 -3 -3, output -3 -2, failed; TC5 input 0 -2 0 3 4 4, output -2 0 3 4, failed. Which of the following provides the BEST description of the failure that can be used in a defect report?
o: The system fails to sort several sets of numbers. Reference: TC3, TC4, TC5.
The system seems to disregard duplicates while sorting. Reference: TC3, TC4, TC5.
The system fails to sort negative numbers. Reference: TC4, TC5.
TC3, TC4 and TC5 have defects (duplicate input data) and should be corrected.
questions.e: In TC3, TC4 and TC5 every duplicate is dropped from the output, so the most useful description is that the function disregards duplicates, which points the developer straight at the likely defect.

questions.q:
Match the descriptions (1-4) with the test tool categories (A-D):
1. Support workflow tracking
2. Facilitate communication
3. Virtual machines
4. Support reviews
A. Static testing tools
B. Tools supporting scalability and deployment standardization
C. DevOps tools
D. Collaboration tools
questions.e: Workflow tracking belongs to DevOps tools (1C), facilitating communication to collaboration tools (2D), virtual machines to scalability and deployment standardization tools (3B), and review support to static testing tools (4A).

questions.q: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a benefit of test automation?
o: It provides coverage measures that are too complicated for humans to derive
It shares responsibility for the testing with the tool vendor
It removes the need for critical thinking when analyzing test results
It generates test cases from an analysis of the program code
questions.e: Tools can derive coverage measures that are impractical for people to compute by hand. Responsibility for testing stays with the testers, critical thinking is still needed, and tools cannot invent expected results from the code alone.
